sources.notes: Regional tourism page; used for limestone cliffs, gorges and long-route character.

sections.heading: Hero
sections.body: A southeast France gorge-and-river destination for limestone and granite climbing, family-friendly outdoor days and spring or autumn conditions.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body:
Ardeche is a regional outdoor destination rather than a single sport crag. The climbing sits in a landscape of cliffs, gorges and river valleys, with the broader trip often mixing climbing with canoeing, canyoning and family-friendly rest days.

For Rockbusters, the useful angle is a practical French climbing holiday: enough climbing variety for sport, multi-pitch and bouldering, but with the rest of the region carrying as much weight as the crags themselves.

sections.heading: Rock and climbing character
sections.body:
The structured rock types are limestone and granite. The clearest public climbing character is limestone cliffs and gorge climbing, with the wider region adding a broader mixed-climbing profile.

Because this is a regional entry, the exact style depends on the chosen valley or crag. Keep the first trip plan broad until individual sectors are chosen from a current topo.

sections.heading: Who it suits
sections.body: Ardeche is well suited to family climbing holidays and mixed-activity groups. It works when not everyone wants to climb every day, because canoeing, canyoning and river-valley tourism sit naturally beside the climbing.

sections.heading: Grades and difficulty
sections.body: The only supported grade wording in this batch is all difficulties, so the file does not infer a numeric grade range. Treat that as a broad suitability signal, not a substitute for a current topo.

sections.heading: Season and conditions
sections.body: Spring and autumn are the supported climbing seasons. Summer is marked as an avoid season for serious climbing because heat can dominate the gorges and cliffs.

sections.heading: Gear and equipment
sections.body: Bring standard sport or multi-pitch equipment based on the chosen crag, and keep water and heat management central outside the shoulder seasons. No destination-specific rack rule was verified in this batch.
warnings: No sourced gear and equipment content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Transport and access
sections.body: Avignon, Nimes and Lyon are the practical airport cities for this region. A car is recommended because the climbing, lodging and rest-day activities are spread out.

sections.heading: Where to stay
sections.body: Campsites, guesthouses and hotels are the supported accommodation picture. In high season, reservations matter because Ardeche is a major outdoor-holiday region, not only a climbing area.

sections.heading: Rest days
sections.body: Canoeing and canyoning are the obvious rest-day activities. The river-gorge setting makes it easy to build a trip where climbing days alternate with water, shade and family-friendly outdoor time.

sections.heading: Practical tips
sections.body: Plan Ardeche as a region. Choose the base around the crags and rest-day activities you actually want, then use a car to keep days flexible.
warnings: No sourced practical tips content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Safety notes
sections.body: Summer heat is the main planning risk. For gorge and river days, keep water, shade and local activity conditions in the plan rather than treating them as extras.

sections.heading: FAQ
sections.body:
Is Ardeche one climbing area? No. It is a regional outdoor destination with multiple climbing and activity bases.

What seasons work best? Spring and autumn.

Is it good for families? Yes. The river-gorge setting works well for trips that mix climbing with canoeing, canyoning and rest-day activities.
